steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“Today” is Saturday **2026-10-24**. Submissions close **six days from today**, i.e., on **Friday 2026-10-30**. The time is **11:59 PM PT** (Pacific Time). Madrid in late October uses **CEST (UTC+2)**, while PT is **PDT (UTC−7)** (since October 30 is after daylight saving starts in the US). The difference is **9 hours** ahead in Madrid, so:

11:59 PM (PT) + 9 hours = **08:59 AM** next day? Actually adding 9 hours to 23:59 gives **32:59**, which is **09:59 AM** the following day—so it becomes **Saturday 2026-10-31 at 09:59 (Madrid time)**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 09:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time (CET) on 30 Oct 2026 (UTC+1). Los Angeles is on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC−7) on that date (since DST ends in early November).  

“Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time” refers to **Monday, 2 Nov 2026, 10:00 AM PDT**. Converting to Madrid time: PDT → CET is +8 hours, so it becomes **18:00 on 2 Nov 2026** in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid in late October uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). The hackathon starts Saturday, 2026-10-24 at 18:00, and lasts 48 hours, so it ends exactly 2 days later at 18:00 on 2026-10-26.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Oct 26, 2026 10:00 AM PT corresponds to Oct 26, 2026 07:00 PM UTC (because PT in late October is UTC-7). Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) then, so local time is 09:00 PM on Oct 26, 2026. Submissions close exactly 72 hours later: that is Oct 29, 2026 at 09:00 PM local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close on **October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET**. Converting ET to Madrid (Spain) on that date: Madrid is **6 hours ahead** of ET (ET is in standard time then). So closing time in Madrid is **November 1, 2026 at 05:59 AM**. Results are announced **exactly 36 hours after submissions close**, i.e. **36 hours after 05:59 AM** = **November 2, 2026 at 17:59 (5:59 PM)**.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

A Unix timestamp of **1791788340** seconds corresponds to **2026-10-11 02:59 (UTC)**. Tokyo (JST) is **UTC+09:00**, so the local time is **2026-10-11 11:59**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 11:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in October 2026, so convert from 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z to local time by adding 2 hours → 2026-10-25 04:30.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Time is 8 hours behind Madrid in standard time (Madrid is CEST in late October, and Pacific Time is PDT until Nov 1, 2026). The last Sunday of October 2026 is **2026-10-25**.  
11:59 PM Pacific Time on 2026-10-25 corresponds to **07:59** the next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Peru (Lima) is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC−5 year-round (no daylight saving).  
In 2026, the US observes the end of daylight saving time on **Sunday, November 1, 2026**, when clocks “fall back” at 2:00 AM local US time (ET). After that switch, Eastern Time becomes **EST = UTC−5**, matching Peru.

The contest deadline is **12:00 noon Eastern Time** on that day, so at that moment Eastern and Peru are both UTC−5, meaning the local time in Lima is also **12:00 noon**.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“AoE” means Anywhere on Earth, i.e., the deadline is at 24:00 AoE = 23:59:59 UTC−12 (last time zone on Earth).  
Tokyo (JST, UTC+9) is 21 hours ahead of UTC−12, so add 21 hours to the UTC−12 time: December 31, 2026 24:00 AoE → January 1, 2027 21:00 in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid in early October follows CEST (UTC+2). New York in early October follows EDT (UTC-4).  
“5:00 PM Sydney time (UTC+10)” on Oct 5, 2026 is at 09:00 UTC. Converting to Madrid (UTC+2) gives 11:00 on Oct 5, 2026.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 11:00
